ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A rectangular board of 8 columns has squared numbered beginning in the upper left corner and moving left to right so row one is numbered 1 through 8, row two is 9 through 16, and so on.  A student shades square 1, then skips one square and shades square 3, skips two squares and shades square 6, skips 3 squares and shades square 10, and continues in this way until there is at least one shaded square in each column.  What is the number of the shaded square that first achieves this result?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows that this is a square grid board with 8 columns in each row, numbered from left to right and from top to bottom; the already blackened squares correspond to the positions 1, 3, 6, 10, etc. given in the problem, indicating that the coloring sequence is consistent with the problem statement. The sequence of colored squares is: first color 1, then successively increase by 2, 3, 4, ..., so the nth colored square is the triangular number T_n = n(n+1)/2. Since each row has 8 columns, the column where number N is located is ((N-1) mod 8)+1; equivalently, when N mod 8 is 1,2,...,7,0, they respectively correspond to columns 1,2,...,7,8. Calculate T_n mod 8 in order: 1, 3, 6, 2, 7, 5, 4, 4, 5, 7, 2, 6, 3, 1, 0. The columns covered by the first 14 remainders are 1, 3, 6, 2, 7, 5, 4, and column 8 is not yet included. The 15th remainder is 0, corresponding to column 8. At this time T_15 = 15×16/2 = 120, so when every column has at least one colored square for the first time, the number of the colored square is 120.

method.method_draft: Use the text to identify the shaded-square sequence as triangular numbers: the 1st shaded square is 1, then differences are 2, 3, 4, etc., so the nth shaded square is T_n = n(n+1)/2. Use the board layout from the image/text to map square numbers to columns by reducing modulo 8: square N is in column ((N-1) mod 8)+1, with multiples of 8 in column 8. Compute T_n modulo 8 in order: 1, 3, 6, 2, 7, 5, 4, 4, 5, 7, 2, 6, 3, 1, 0. These cover columns 1, 3, 6, 2, 7, 5, 4, and finally column 8 at T_15 = 120. Therefore the first shaded square that gives at least one shaded square in each column is 120.

method.method_draft: Track only columns rather than full square numbers. From the image/text, the board repeats columns every 8 squares. Starting at square 1, the shaded column is column 1. Each new shaded square is reached by moving forward 2 squares, then 3 squares, then 4 squares, etc.; modulo 8, this advances the column by 2, 3, 4, etc. Starting column sequence is therefore: 1, then 1+2=3, then 3+3=6, then 6+4=10≡2, then +5 gives 7, then +6 gives 5, then +7 gives 4, then +8 stays 4, then +9 gives 5, then +10 gives 7, then +11 gives 2, then +12 gives 6, then +13 gives 3, then +14 gives 1, then +15 gives 8. Column 8 first appears on the 15th shaded square, so compute the actual 15th shaded square by adding the jumps or using T_15 = 15·16/2 = 120.
